headline: High-risk data and capability overlap: TREK’s collaborative, MCP-enabled planner can conflict with slim’s broad filesystem/container control, creating default-path leakage and cascading misuse risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: TREK uses MCP and real-time collaboration, so its outputs can be bridged into slim’s interactive CLI workflow if an operator copies or pipes content. slim reads/writes filesystem artifacts and executes shell commands, making it plausible to treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred from both profiles.
conditions: IF TREK output is copied into slim prompts or shell commands
IF a shared MCP or file bridge is configured between the two agents
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of agent output into commands
Use a read-only handoff file with strict templates
Add an operator review step before any shell execution
requires-engineering: enforce provenance tags on bridged content

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK touches reservations, documents, photos, API keys, and MFA secrets, while slim handles filesystem artifacts, certificate private keys, environment variables, and registry credentials. slim has broad network egress and filesystem access, so if both share a workspace or handoff files, sensitive TREK data can be exposed or exfiltrated. The pairwise path is not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same workspace or upload directory
IF TREK secrets or documents are written into files slim can access
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Store secrets outside shared directories
Rotate any exposed API keys or MFA secrets
Restrict slim egress to required registries only
requires-engineering: add per-agent access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: slim can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, and TREK is collaborative with multiple instances and mutable files such as ./data/travel.db and ./uploads/. If both operate on the same mutable resources, concurrent writes can corrupt state or overwrite each other. No locking or isolation is documented, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or database
IF TREK’s collaborative sessions and slim’s file writes overlap in time
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories per agent
Pause one agent during the other’s write phase
Back up mutable files before runs
Use file locks around shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in, so its outputs may be treated as actionable travel advice. slim can execute shell commands and manipulate container artifacts, but its profile does not show direct downstream action-taking like email or booking. The main risk is that TREK’s output becomes slim’s input without verification, causing incorrect operational steps.
conditions: IF slim consumes TREK-generated instructions without human review
IF TREK outputs are used as commands or configuration for slim
mitigations: Require human approval before acting on TREK output
Validate TREK outputs against a schema
Log and diff any generated commands before execution
Use a second-pass verifier for high-impact steps

E_compliance.rationale: TREK handles user accounts, email addresses, reservations, API keys, and MFA secrets, while slim handles registry credentials and certificate private keys. Both profiles are docs-only and open-source, but their data classes imply different retention and secret-handling obligations. No residency or certification mismatch is explicit, so this is a moderate compliance-risk inference rather than a confirmed breach.
conditions: IF the deployment stores EU PII or regulated secrets in TREK and passes them to slim
IF retention or logging policies differ between the two systems
mitigations: Minimize sensitive fields shared between agents
Review logging settings for secrets
Set explicit retention limits for shared artifacts
Document data-flow boundaries for operators
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
